1	# GH3 (Wii) — Navigation Model
2	
3	Working model of Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (Wii) screens and the menu
4	graph between them. This is the source artifact for the §4.8 game-state work:
5	the **observer** (M9) classifies the current screen and reads the highlighted
6	selection; the **controller** (M10) plans button sequences along the graph
7	edges below. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.8.3 (game catalog & menu metadata).
8	
9	Screen text is transcribed from operator narration; the referenced screens live
10	as a renamed corpus in [`gh3_screens/`](gh3_screens/) (see its README for the
11	name ↔ original-snapshot mapping). Raw `marvin-perf snapshot` captures land in
12	the gitignored `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/`. Native capture is 720×480.
13	
14	**Scope now:** the navigation *structure* — screens, their items, and the edges
15	between them. The **vision** side (per-screen classifier regions, highlight
16	readout) is deferred until the observer (M9) is built; screen snapshots are
17	recorded here now so that work has its corpus ready.
18	
19	Status: **in progress** — populated screen-by-screen. `TBD` = not yet captured.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Conventions
24	
25	### Inputs
26	- **Strum up / strum down** — move the selection within a list.
27	- **GREEN** — confirm / enter the selected item.
28	- **RED** — back up one level.
29	
30	(Bit names on the wire are the gameplay fret/strum masks; the controller emits
31	the same bits for menu navigation — the fretboard MCU doesn't distinguish menu
32	from gameplay. §4.8.4.) Some menus also use the `+` button (pause) and possibly
33	others beyond fret/strum; the full controller is actuatable in principle —
34	fauxmote emulates the complete guitar extension incl. `+`/`−` — the actuator
35	command protocol just needs to carry those inputs.
36	
37	### Highlight paradigms
38	How "selected" is presented drives what the observer reads. Two kinds so far:
39	
40	- **static-list** — the list is painted at fixed screen positions; a highlight
41	  moves between rows. Observer reads *which row is lit*. (e.g. `main_menu`)
42	- **fixed-slot** — the selected item sits in a fixed, highlighted slot and the
43	  list scrolls underneath it. Observer reads *what occupies the highlight slot*.
44	  (e.g. `song_select`)
45	
46	### Edge notation
47	An edge is `from → to : [inputs]`. `STRUM_DN×n` means n strum-downs. Moving to
48	list index `i` from the top (index 0) on a static list is `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN`.
49

86	- **snapshot:** `gh3_screens/tutorials_menu.png`
87	- **reached from:** `training_menu` → TUTORIALS
88	- Not modeling the tutorials path. **Recovery:** if the controller lands here by

91	### song_select  *(shared node)*
92	- **snapshot:** `gh3_screens/song_select__00_slow_ride.png` (first song "Slow Ride" selected)
93	- **reached from:** `training_menu` → PRACTICE. Expected to be the **same screen**
94	  reused by other modes (CAREER, QUICKPLAY) — confirm as those paths are walked.
95	- **paradigm:** fixed-slot (selection fixed on screen; song list scrolls under it)
96	- **items:** see [Song catalog](#song-catalog-main-setlist) below; index 0 = "Slow Ride".
97	- **select song i:** `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` (from the top of the list).
98	- **BLUE fret:** toggle to the **bonus** setlist; **YELLOW** returns to the main setlist.
99	- **back (RED):** returns to the entering menu (path-dependent — `training_menu`
100	  on this path).
101	- **leads to:** `part_select` (may be skipped for some songs — TBD).
102	- **note:** assumed identical across modes; when walking CAREER, verify the
103	  *song set* matches (tiers / locked songs may differ even if the layout is shared).
104	
105	### part_select  *(variable — song-dependent)*
106	- **reached from:** `song_select` → GREEN on a song.
107	- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves).
108	- **items:** **song-dependent** — the offered parts vary by song. Observed:
109	  - `{ LEAD (0), RHYTHM (1) }` — `gh3_screens/part_select__lead.png` (LEAD sel), `gh3_screens/part_select__rhythm.png` (RHYTHM sel)
110	  - `{ LEAD, BASS }` reported for other songs — no snapshot yet
111	  - the screen **may not appear at all** for some songs (TBD which).
112	- **select:** LEAD = `GREEN`; second item = `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` (assumes LEAD is
113	  always index 0 — confirm).
114	- **back (RED):** `song_select`
115	- **leads to:** `difficulty_select`.
116	- **note:** because the item set varies per song *and* the screen may be absent,
117	  the navigator can't hardcode this step. It needs either per-song "available
118	  parts" metadata (candidate: a `parts` column on the song catalog) or a live
119	  screen read (vision, M9).

121	### difficulty_select
122	- **reached from:** `part_select` → GREEN on a part.
123	- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves).
124	- **items (top → bottom, index; snapshot = that item selected):**
125	  0. EASY — `gh3_screens/difficulty__easy.png`
126	  1. MEDIUM — `gh3_screens/difficulty__medium.png`
127	  2. HARD — `gh3_screens/difficulty__hard.png`

129	- **select:** `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` (EASY=0 … EXPERT=3).
130	- **back (RED):** `part_select`
131	- **leads to:** `section_select`.
132	- **note:** likely the same difficulty screen used by other modes (CAREER,
133	  QUICKPLAY) — treat as a candidate shared node when those paths are walked.
134	  Default selection on entry may be sticky (last-used) rather than always EASY —

136	
137	### section_select  *(practice — variable per song)*
138	- **reached from:** `difficulty_select` → GREEN.
139	- **paradigm:** static-list (assumed; confirm).
140	- **items:** **song-dependent** (intro / verse / solo / etc.), but **index 0 is
141	  always "FULL SONG"** — `gh3_screens/section_select__full_song.png`. Only FULL SONG is in scope; other
142	  sections are ignored.
143	- **select FULL SONG:** `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` — strum up to the **top** of the
144	  list (FULL SONG = index 0), then confirm. Don't assume the cursor enters at
145	  index 0 (may be sticky / land elsewhere); strumming up saturates at the top so
146	  it lands on FULL SONG regardless of entry position. `N` ≥ the longest section
147	  list (or "until the highlight stops moving"). **Assumes no wrap-around** — see
148	  open items; if the list wraps, read the highlight instead.
149	- **back (RED):** `difficulty_select`.
150	- **leads to:** `speed_select`.

152	### speed_select
153	- **reached from:** `section_select` → FULL SONG.
154	- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves).
155	- **items (top → bottom, index; snapshot = that item selected):**
156	  0. FULL SPEED — `gh3_screens/speed__full_speed.png`
157	  1. SLOW — `gh3_screens/speed__slow.png`
158	  2. SLOWER — `gh3_screens/speed__slower.png`
159	  3. SLOWEST — `gh3_screens/speed__slowest.png`
160	- **select FULL SPEED:** `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` — same top-saturating approach as
161	  FULL SONG above (FULL SPEED = index 0); robust to a sticky default.
162	- **back (RED):** `section_select`.
163	- **leads to:** `loading`.
164	
165	### loading  *(transient — no input)*
166	- **screen:** `gh3_screens/loading.png`
167	- **reached from:** `speed_select` (final selection), and on RESTART from
168	  `practice_end_menu`.
169	- Not a menu — the song is loading. The navigator **waits** here (no inputs);
170	  it auto-advances to `in_song`. The observer should recognize it so the
171	  controller holds instead of mis-firing into the next screen.
172	- **leads to:** `in_song`.
173	
174	### in_song  *(gameplay)*
175	- **reached from:** `loading`.
176	- **screen:** `gh3_screens/in_song__training.png` (training-mode example).
177	- The song plays; this is the `gameplay` state where note detection (§4.2,
178	  cv_marvin_v1) takes over. Not a menu. **Background is mode-dependent** — the
179	  training background is always the same; other modes (career/quickplay) may use
180	  different backgrounds, which matters for the observer's `gameplay` classifier.
181	- **pause:** the guitar `+` button opens `pause_menu` mid-song.
182	- **leads to:** `pause_menu` (via `+`), or `practice_end_menu` (when the song
183	  finishes).
184	
185	### pause_menu  *(mid-song overlay)*
186	- **reached from:** `in_song` → `+` (guitar plus/pause button).
187	- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves; confirm).
188	- **items (top → bottom, index; snapshot = that item selected):**
189	  0. RESUME — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__resume.png`
190	  1. RESTART — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__restart.png`
191	  2. OPTIONS — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__options.png`
192	  3. CHANGE SPEED — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__change_speed.png`
193	  4. CHANGE SECTION — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__change_section.png`
194	  5. NEW SONG — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__new_song.png`
195	  6. QUIT — `gh3_screens/pause_menu__quit.png`
196	- **select:** `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN`.
197	- **back (RED):** TBD (likely resumes — confirm).
198	- **leads to:**
199	  - RESUME → `in_song` (resume gameplay)
200	  - RESTART → `loading` → `in_song` (replay current song)
201	  - OPTIONS → options submenu *(out of scope; RED to recover)*
202	  - CHANGE SPEED → `speed_select`
203	  - CHANGE SECTION → `section_select`
204	  - NEW SONG → `song_select`
205	  - QUIT → `quit_confirm` (confirmation dialog — not straight to main menu)
206	- **`+` actuation:** opening the pause needs the `+` button (not a fret/strum
207	  bit). Actuatable in principle — fauxmote's emulated guitar-extension report
208	  already carries the `+`/`−` buttons ([`firmware/fauxmote`](../../fauxmote/SPEC.md),
209	  §3). The marvin→actuator command path is fret/strum-focused today (§4.3);
210	  carrying `+`/`−` and other controller buttons for menu use is a command-protocol
211	  extension, not a hardware limit.
212	
213	### quit_confirm  *(confirmation dialog)*
214	- **reached from:** `pause_menu` → QUIT (and possibly other QUIT actions — see
215	  `practice_end_menu`).
216	- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves; confirm).
217	- **items (top → bottom, index; snapshot = that item selected):**
218	  0. CANCEL — `gh3_screens/quit_confirm__cancel.png`
219	  1. QUIT — `gh3_screens/quit_confirm__quit.png`
220	- **select:** CANCEL = `GREEN`; QUIT = `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN`.
221	- **back (RED):** likely = CANCEL (returns to `pause_menu`) — confirm.
222	- **leads to:**
223	  - CANCEL → `pause_menu` (back, no quit)
224	  - QUIT → `main_menu`
225	- **note:** safe default is CANCEL (index 0); a "confirm quit" plan must
226	  explicitly `STRUM_DN×1` to QUIT, not assume the cursor starts there.

375	## Navigator notes (implementation)
376	
377	How the controller (M10) uses this map. Unmapped paths don't need modeling —
378	they're handled by recovery, not enumeration.
379	
380	- **Closed-loop — verify every screen (not a blind macro).** Before issuing a
381	  step's inputs, confirm the observer reports the expected screen; after issuing
382	  them, confirm the expected destination before proceeding. On mismatch, recover
383	  (see below) and re-plan. Never fire a button sequence open-loop and *assume* we
384	  landed where we hoped — drift, sticky defaults, variable/absent screens, and
385	  load times all break that. This is why the observer (M9) gates the controller
386	  (M10). (spec §4.8.1.)
387	- **Stubs / unknown destinations.** Edges marked `TBD` simply have no plan; the
388	  navigator never routes through them. Out-of-scope nodes (`tutorials_menu`) and
389	  any screen the observer doesn't recognize are treated as "unknown state."
390	- **Recovery from unknown state.** RED backs up one level from any menu, so the
391	  generic recovery is *"press RED until a recognized screen appears, then
392	  re-plan."* This gets us un-stuck from a wrong branch without mapping it.
393	- **Top-item selection (`STRUM_UP×N`).** For steps where we always want the top
394	  item (FULL SONG, FULL SPEED), strum up to saturate at the top, then GREEN,
395	  rather than trusting the entry highlight. (Depends on no wrap-around — open.)
396	
397	### Worked path — training run (main-setlist song `i`, difficulty `d`, LEAD)
398	The nominal input plan. Each step runs **gated on a screen check** (verify the
399	expected screen before, confirm arrival after) per the closed-loop rule above —
400	it is not executed as one blind burst. From `main_menu` (if not there, recover
401	with RED first):
402	
403	1. `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` → TRAINING → `training_menu`
404	2. `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` → PRACTICE → `song_select`
405	3. `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` → song at catalog index `i` (Song catalog) → `part_select`
406	4. select LEAD, then GREEN → `difficulty_select`  *(see caveat)*
407	5. `STRUM_DN×d, GREEN` → difficulty `d` (EASY 0 … EXPERT 3) → `section_select`
408	6. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SONG → `speed_select`
409	7. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SPEED → `loading` (wait) → `in_song` (gameplay)
410	
411	**Caveat (step 4):** `part_select` items vary per song and the screen may be
412	absent — exactly the case the closed-loop rule handles: after step 3's GREEN,
413	check which screen actually appeared. If it's `part_select`, pick LEAD (read the
414	offered items) and GREEN; if it's already `difficulty_select`, skip step 4. A
415	purely open-loop macro can't do this safely (extra inputs would mis-fire), so
416	until the observer exists, restrict to songs known to show LEAD-at-top. Per-song
417	`parts` metadata lets the planner pre-know the layout either way.

The public `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API and all perf-log records (FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE stamps, ACTUATOR, FRETBOARD_RAW) are unchanged, so `timing_pipeline`/`manual_control` and host `marvin-perf` need no edits. | The link is unchanged at the fretboard end (always SERCOM1 UART @ 500 000); only marvin's side was USB-bridged. Ring-buffer mode chosen over the basic single-transfer plib because the fretboard streams 17-byte frames continuously at 240 Hz: the basic plib disables RXRDY between a completed Read and the next arm, risking overrun, whereas the ring fills from its own ISR with no gap. RX is now a simple drain — a persistent read-threshold (`DS_FRAME_LEN`) notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which pulls bytes off the ring and runs the same `0x03 … 0xFC` resync as before; the separate `s_rx_stream` stream buffer + ISR re-arm are deleted (the ring *is* the buffer). TX drops the USB Write/ack-semaphore dance: a ring-buffer `Write` copies the byte and returns, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. No enumeration/attach/detach → `s_connected` becomes a static `s_link_up`. The `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` perf-stage name is now historical (it's a UART enqueue) but kept to avoid a host-decoder schema change. |

An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)

Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.

Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*

The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.

EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.

MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
134	     ```c
135	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
136	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
137	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
138	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
139	     ```
140	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.

144	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). 145	
146	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
147	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
148	
149	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. ```text
403	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
404	
405	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
406	
407	#### 4.8.1 Role
408	
409	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
410	
411	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
413	
414	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
415	
416	Recognition is being bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, the detection algorithms (screen classification, then number/letter/score region readers) are prototyped host-side in Python against that corpus, and only the proven, simple GH3-specific logic is then ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
417	
418	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
419	
420	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
421	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
422	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
423	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
424	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
425	
426	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
427	
428	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
429	
430	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
431	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
432	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
433	
434	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
435	
436	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
437	
438	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
439	
440	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
441	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
442	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
443	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
444	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
445	
446	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
447	
448	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
449	
450	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
451	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
452	
453	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
454	
455	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
456	
457	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). The console is instead a small in-tree module (`console/console.{h,c}`) in the same shape as `fretboard_link`/`perf_log`: it owns the USART plib directly, is fully statically allocated, and is kept out of MCC via `user.cmake`.
458	- **Library:** [embedded-cli](https://github.com/funbiscuit/embedded-cli) (vendored under `default/src/third_party/embedded-cli/`, MIT), used in static-allocation mode (a fixed `CLI_UINT` buffer → no `malloc`). Provides line editing, history, and tab-completion.
459	- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
460	- **Commands (v0):** `status`, `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>`, `active <cv|adc>`, `timing <on|off>`, `manual <on|off>`, `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>`, `strum <down|up>` — dispatching into the existing `Detector_*`, `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled`, and `ManualControl_*` setters. The binding table is a plain static array; adding a command is one row. Maps onto the §6 operating-mode toggles. (`record`/`game_*` toggles and runtime timing-constant setters are deferred until those subsystems / setters exist.)
461	
462	---
463	
464	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
465	
466	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
467	
468	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
469	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
470	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
471	
472	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
473	
474	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
475	
476	| Toggle | Effect |
477	|---|---|
478	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
479	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
480	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
481	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
482	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
483	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
484	
485	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
486	
487	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
488	
489	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
490	
491	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
492	
493	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
494	
495	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
496	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
497	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
498	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
499	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
500	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
501	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
502	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
503	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
504	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
505	
506	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.
507	
508	## 9. Open questions
509	
510	| # | Question | Status |
511	|---|---|---|
512	| Q1 | Reference-data format details — keyframe stride and per-fret patch sizes if patches are added later. | Direction set (§4.6.3); exact stride defaults to 60 frames, revisit after first training-data consumer exists. |
513	| Q2 | Reference-data transport beyond SD — Ethernet live stream timing. | Deferred post-M8. |
514	| Q3 | Detector-state bus shape — typed messages on a queue (§4.2.4) is the working choice; revisit if multi-consumer latency becomes a problem. | Working choice. |
515	| Q4 | Timing pipeline location — marvin centralized with fretboard fallback. | Settled; implementation in M3 + M8. |
516	| Q5 | UI framework — Legato vs custom on GFX2D. | Open. Decide at M5. |
517	| Q6 | Operating-mode model — independent toggles. | Settled (§6). |
518	| Q7 | Fret-tuner's long-term fate — survives as off-band dev/calibration tool. | Settled; not in runtime path. |
519	| Q8 | Initial CV algorithm choice for `cv_marvin_v1`. | Open. Decide at M1. |
520	| Q9 | Config persistence location (SD file vs internal flash). | Open. Decide at M4 alongside SDMMC bring-up. |
521	| Q10 | Game-state recognizer algorithm — template matching vs OCR vs color/region heuristics vs small CNN. | Open. Decide at M9; revisit if first algorithm misclassifies on real game UI. |
522	| Q11 | Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline (§4.4 vs §4.8). Default working assumption: mutually exclusive (controller runs only outside `gameplay` state); may need richer arbitration if a game has gameplay-screen menus or pause overlays we want to drive. | Open. Decide at M10. |

```text
1	"""Reassemble PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT band strips into a full frame and save it.
2	
3	The device answers a snapshot command with a top-to-bottom run of full-width
4	`STRIP` records (kind SNAPSHOT), all sharing one `frame_epoch`; the final band
5	sets `STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. This module groups bands by `frame_epoch`, pastes them
6	onto a canvas, and writes the result as a lossless `.png` (frame_epoch in a
7	tEXt chunk).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from .records import STRIP_BPP, Strip, StripKind
16	
17	
18	@dataclass(frozen=True)
19	class CompletedSnapshot:
20	    width: int
21	    height: int
22	    frame_epoch: int
23	    bgr: bytes  # width * height * 3, row-major, top-to-bottom
24	
25	    @property
26	    def n_bytes(self) -> int:
27	        return self.width * self.height * STRIP_BPP
28	
29	
30	class SnapshotError(Exception):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class _Pending:
36	    width: int
37	    bands: dict[int, Strip] = field(default_factory=dict)  # keyed by band y
38	    last_y: int | None = None  # y of the band flagged LAST
39	
40	
41	class SnapshotAssembler:
42	    """Feed decoded `Strip` records; get a `CompletedSnapshot` when done.
43	
44	    `add()` ignores non-SNAPSHOT strips and returns None until a snapshot's
45	    LAST band has arrived and every row from 0..height is covered, at which
46	    point it returns the assembled frame (and forgets that frame_epoch).
47	    """
48	
49	    def __init__(self) -> None:
50	        self._pending: dict[int, _Pending] = {}
51	
52	    def add(self, strip: Strip) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
53	        if strip.kind != int(StripKind.SNAPSHOT):
54	            return None
55	        if strip.x != 0:
56	            raise SnapshotError(f"snapshot band at x={strip.x}, expected full-width")
57	
58	        epoch = strip.hdr.frame_epoch
59	        p = self._pending.get(epoch)
60	        if p is None:
61	            p = _Pending(width=strip.w)
62	            self._pending[epoch] = p
63	        elif strip.w != p.width:
64	            raise SnapshotError(
65	                f"snapshot band width {strip.w} != {p.width} (frame_epoch {epoch})"
66	            )
67	
68	        p.bands[strip.y] = strip
69	        if strip.is_last:
70	            p.last_y = strip.y
71	
72	        if p.last_y is None:
73	            return None
74	        return self._try_finalize(epoch, p)
75	
76	    def _try_finalize(self, epoch: int, p: _Pending) -> CompletedSnapshot | None:
77	        # Walk contiguous bands from y=0; bail (keep waiting) on any gap.
78	        canvas = bytearray()
79	        y = 0
80	        height = 0
81	        while y in p.bands:
82	            band = p.bands[y]
83	            canvas += band.bgr
84	            height = y + band.h
85	            y += band.h
86	        if p.last_y is None or height <= p.last_y:
87	            return None  # not yet contiguous through the LAST band
88	
89	        del self._pending[epoch]
90	        return CompletedSnapshot(
91	            width=p.width, height=height, frame_epoch=epoch, bgr=bytes(canvas)
92	        )
93	
94	
95	def save_snapshot(snap: CompletedSnapshot, out: str | Path) -> list[Path]:
96	    """Write the snapshot as a lossless PNG and return its path.
97	
98	    `out` may carry a .png suffix (or a stale .bgr/.json, stripped) or be a bare
99	    stem; the result is always `<stem>.png`. PNG is lossless for the packed RGB
100	    pixels, so no separate raw buffer is needed; `frame_epoch` rides along in a
101	    tEXt chunk rather than a sidecar JSON.
102	    """
103	    base = Path(out)
104	    if base.suffix.lower() in (".bgr", ".png", ".json"):
105	        base = base.with_suffix("")
106	    base.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
107	
108	    try:
109	        from PIL import Image, PngImagePlugin
110	    except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover - Pillow is a base dependency
111	        raise SnapshotError("Pillow is required to save snapshots as PNG") from e
112	
113	    # Pillow's "raw" decoder maps BGR → RGB without a manual per-pixel swap.
114	    img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (snap.width, snap.height), snap.bgr, "raw", "BGR")
115	    meta = PngImagePlugin.PngInfo()
116	    meta.add_text("frame_epoch", str(snap.frame_epoch))
117	
118	    png_path = base.with_suffix(".png")
119	    img.save(png_path, pnginfo=meta)
120	    return [png_path]
121
```

40	# ─── Type-mask CLI parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	
42	
43	def parse_types_arg(spec: str | None) -> int | None:
44	    """Resolve a `--types` spec to a u32 mask. Returns None if `spec` is None.
45	
46	    Accepts a comma-separated list of RecordType names plus the special tokens
47	    `ALL` (0xFFFFFFFF) and `MIN` (SESSION|DROP). Case-insensitive.
48	    """
49	    if spec is None:
50	        return None
51	    mask = 0
52	    for raw in spec.split(","):
53	        token = raw.strip().upper()
54	        if not token:
55	            continue
56	        if token == "ALL":
57	            return TYPE_MASK_ALL
58	        if token == "MIN":
59	            mask |= TYPE_MASK_MIN
60	            continue
61	        if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
62	            valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
63	            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
64	                f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL, MIN"
65	            )
66	        mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
67	    return mask
68	
69	
70	def _types_help() -> str:
71	    bit_lines = ", ".join(
72	        f"{name}={int(rt)}" for name, rt in sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME.items())
73	    )
74	    return (
75	        "Comma-separated record types to enable on the device. "
76	        f"Names: {bit_lines}. Special: ALL (default), MIN (SESSION+DROP). "
77	        "SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask. Old firmware ignores the command."
78	    )

81	def _send_mask(ser: SerialSource, mask: int) -> None:
82	    payload = encode_set_mask_payload(mask)
83	    ser.send_command(frame_encode(payload))
84	    print(f"[mask] sent 0x{mask:08x}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

90	def cmd_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
91	    """Pure pass-through to disk; no decode.
92	
93	    Two modes: `--out FILE.bin` writes a raw legacy file; `--out-dir DIR`
94	    writes a capture directory (DIR/perf.bin + manifest.json finalized on
95	    close).
96	    """
97	    if (args.out is None) == (args.out_dir is None):
98	        print("record: exactly one of --out or --out-dir is required", file=sys.stderr)
99	        return 2
100	
101	    if args.out_dir is not None:
102	        cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)
103	        bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
104	        label = f"capture {cap_dir.name}/"
105	    else:
106	        cap_dir = None
107	        bin_path = Path(args.out)
108	        label = f"recording {bin_path.name}"
109	
110	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)
111	    bytes_written = 0
112	    last_status = time.monotonic()
113	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser, bin_path.open("wb") as fh:
114	        if mask is not None:
115	            _send_mask(ser, mask)
116	        try:
117	            for chunk in ser:
118	                fh.write(chunk)
119	                fh.flush()
120	                bytes_written += len(chunk)
121	                now = time.monotonic()
122	                if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
123	                    print(f"{label}: {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
124	                    last_status = now
125	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
126	            print(f"\nstopped after {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr)
127	
128	    if cap_dir is not None:
129	        manifest = finalize_capture_dir(
130	            cap_dir,
131	            source=CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=args.port),
132	        )
133	        print(
134	            f"finalized {cap_dir}/manifest.json — {manifest.n_records} records, "
135	            f"types={manifest.producer_capabilities}",
136	            file=sys.stderr,
137	        )
138	    return 0

142	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)
143	    if mask is None:
144	        print("set-mask: --types is required", file=sys.stderr)
145	        return 2
146	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:

150	
151	def cmd_set_overlay(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
152	    """Toggle the per-fret target rings on the SENSING strip."""
153	    flags = PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP if args.on else 0
154	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
155	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_overlay_payload(flags)))
156	    print(f"set-overlay: strip rings {'on' if args.on else 'off'}", file=sys.stderr)
157	    return 0

159	
160	def _idle_chunks(ser: SerialSource, idle_timeout_s: float):
161	    """Yield serial chunks until `idle_timeout_s` elapses with no new bytes.
162	
163	    Lets `iter_frames` terminate once the snapshot burst stops (or stalls),
164	    instead of blocking forever on the infinite SerialSource iterator.
165	    """
166	    deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
167	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
168	        chunk = ser.read_chunk()
169	        if chunk:
170	            deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
171	            yield chunk
172	
173	
174	def _resolve_snapshot_out(out: str | None) -> Path:
175	    """Resolve the `--out` argument to a concrete .png path.
176	
177	    A value ending in `.png` is taken literally. Anything else (including the
178	    default when `--out` is omitted) is treated as a directory, and the next
179	    free `snapshot-NNNN.png` in it is chosen so rapid captures never clobber.
180	    """
181	    p = Path(out) if out else Path("snapshots")
182	    if p.suffix.lower() == ".png":
183	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184	        return p
185	
186	    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
187	    nums = [
188	        int(m.group(1))
189	        for f in p.glob("snapshot-*.png")
190	        if (m := re.fullmatch(r"snapshot-(\d+)", f.stem))
191	    ]
192	    nxt = (max(nums) + 1) if nums else 1
193	    return p / f"snapshot-{nxt:04d}.png"

196	def cmd_snapshot(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
197	    """Trigger a full-frame snapshot and save it as a lossless PNG.
198	
199	    Sends PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, reassembles the returned SNAPSHOT band strips into
200	    one frame, and writes a PNG. With `--out` omitted (or pointed at a
201	    directory) the filename auto-increments as `snapshot-NNNN.png` for quick
202	    repeated captures.
203	    """
204	    out_path = _resolve_snapshot_out(args.out)
205	
206	    assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
207	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
208	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))
209	        print("[snapshot] requested; waiting for bands…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
210	        snap = None
211	        for fb in iter_frames(_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)):
212	            rec = decode_record(fb.payload)
213	            if not isinstance(rec, Strip):
214	                continue
215	            snap = assembler.add(rec)
216	            if snap is not None:
217	                break
218	
219	    if snap is None:
220	        print(
221	            f"snapshot: no complete frame within {args.timeout:.1f}s idle timeout. "
222	            "Is marvin connected, HDMI locked, and the firmware schema current?",
223	            file=sys.stderr,
224	        )
225	        return 1
226	
227	    written = save_snapshot(snap, out_path)
228	    print(
229	        f"snapshot: {snap.width}×{snap.height} (frame_epoch {snap.frame_epoch}) → "
230	        + ", ".join(str(p) for p in written),
231	        file=sys.stderr,
232	    )
233	    return 0

```md
# GH3 game-state engine — offline prototype, slice 1: screen classifier

## Context

marvin needs a **game-state observer** (spec §4.8, milestone M9): watch the captured
video and recognize which GH3 screen the game is on (main_menu, song_select,
gameplay, pause, …), so the navigator (M10) can drive menus closed-loop along the
graph in [`gh3_navigation.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md). Per Q10 the
chosen approach is **fixed-region/color fingerprints**, not general CV — GH3's screens
and layouts are static.

The on-ramp work is done: `marvin-perf snapshot` has produced a labelled corpus of 102
real GH3 screens at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (720×480 PNG, 13 screen classes).
We prototype the detection algorithm **host-side in Python against that corpus first**,
prove it, and only later port the proven, simple logic to a firmware `gameplay_engine`
module (out of scope here).

**This slice = the screen classifier only** (not the highlight/selection reader, not the
navigator). Output for a frame: `screen_id` + confidence, or `UNKNOWN` (the navigator's
recovery path depends on a trustworthy UNKNOWN).

**Hard constraint — analog slop.** The Wii emits analog component video that is converted
to HDMI before capture, so any algorithm must tolerate (a) **positional slop** (overscan /
sub-pixel position drift, slight scale) and (b) **value slop** (gain/offset, limited↔full
range, analog noise). The corpus snapshots are *clean digital captures over the perf-log
path* and do **not** contain this slop, so robustness must be validated by injecting
synthetic perturbations. This is why the fingerprint is coarse region-averaged color, not
a pixel-exact template/hash.

**Decisions taken (this planning turn):** new `tools/gameplay/` subproject with its own uv
env + journal; host-only (no firmware-facing template export yet).

## Approach

Coarse **fixed-region mean-color fingerprint** + **nearest-centroid classifier** with an
**UNKNOWN reject** rule, plus an evaluation harness that includes a slop-robustness pass.
Everything is written to mirror cheap integer C (sum pixels per region, divide, L1
compare) so the eventual firmware port is mechanical — but no export is produced yet.

### New subproject layout: `tools/gameplay/`

Mirrors `tools/marvin-perf/` conventions (uv project, `pyproject.toml`, package + `tests/`).

\```
tools/gameplay/
  pyproject.toml            # name="gameplay"; deps: pillow, numpy; dev: pytest; script: gameplay=gameplay.cli:main
  .python-version           # 3.12 (match marvin-perf)
  README.md
  docs/journal.md           # new subproject journal (CLAUDE.md rule 4)
  gameplay/
    __init__.py
    screens.py              # canonical ScreenId set + filename-prefix→id map (aligned with gh3_navigation.md)
    corpus.py               # locate gh3_screens/, load *.png → (screen_id, ndarray); derive label from filename prefix
    fingerprint.py          # region grid + fingerprint(img)->uint8 vector (integer per-region BGR means; C-shaped)
    classifier.py           # build_templates() centroids; classify(fp)->(id, dist, margin); UNKNOWN reject rule
    perturb.py              # synthetic analog-slop: brightness/gain/offset, translate, gaussian noise, scale/overscan crop
    evaluate.py             # LOO CV + confusion matrix + threshold sweep + robustness report
    cli.py                  # `gameplay classify <png>`, `gameplay eval`
  tests/{__init__,conftest,test_screens,test_fingerprint,test_classifier,test_perturb}.py
\```

### `screens.py` — canonical ids + label map

13 ids matching the `gh3_navigation.md` catalog. The filename prefix (before `__`) maps to
the canonical id; two prefixes are renamed to match the nav doc:

- `difficulty` → `difficulty_select`
- `speed` → `speed_select`
- (all others map by identity: `main_menu`, `training_menu`, `tutorials_menu`,
  `song_select` — covers both `__NN_` and `__bonus_NN_` —, `part_select`,
  `section_select`, `loading`, `in_song`, `pause_menu`, `quit_confirm`, `practice_end_menu`)

This module is the single source of truth aligning prototype ids ↔ nav-doc screen names.

### `fingerprint.py` — the fixed-region signature (Q10)

- Resize input to a canonical 720×480 first (defensive against resolution drift).
- Partition into a coarse **G×H grid** (start **8×6 = 48 regions**; grid resolution is a
  swept parameter in eval). Each region → integer mean of (B,G,R). Fingerprint =
  concatenated `uint8` vector, length `3·G·H` (144 at 8×6).
- Coarse averaging is what buys positional-slop tolerance (sub-cell shifts wash out).
- Written as plain accumulate-sum-then-divide over rectangles so it ports 1:1 to integer C.
- Provide an optional per-frame **value-normalization** variant (e.g. subtract global mean
  luma / scale to fixed mean) to combat gain/offset slop; raw-vs-normalized is chosen
  **empirically in eval**, not assumed.

### `classifier.py` — nearest-centroid + UNKNOWN

- Template per class = **centroid** (mean fingerprint over that class's corpus samples).
  K small fixed-size templates (the future firmware metadata; not exported yet).
- `d_k = L1(fp, template_k)`; `best = argmin`, `second = next-smallest`.
- Accept `best` iff `d_best ≤ T_abs` **and** `(d_second − d_best) ≥ T_margin`; else UNKNOWN.
- Integer math throughout. Confidence derived from the margin.
- `song_select` is one class spanning main+bonus setlists; eval will reveal if the bonus
  tab variation hurts the centroid (treat as one class unless eval says otherwise).

### `evaluate.py` — prove it, including slop

1. **Leave-one-out CV** over multi-sample classes → accuracy + confusion matrix.
2. **Single-sample classes** (`loading`, `in_song`, `section_select`, `tutorials_menu`)
   can't LOO — report resubstitution + lean on the robustness pass; flag honestly.
3. **UNKNOWN-rejection test:** hold out an entire class's samples (centroid absent),
   confirm they reject as UNKNOWN — validates `T_abs`/`T_margin`.
4. **Slop-robustness pass (the analog point):** apply `perturb.py` transforms across an
   envelope (brightness/gain ±, offset, ±few-px translate, overscan crop/scale, noise σ)
   and report classification-stability rate + margin degradation per perturbation type.
5. **Threshold selection:** from the separation between in-class `d_best` and
   nearest-wrong-class distance, print recommended `T_abs`, `T_margin`.

### `cli.py`

- `gameplay classify <png>` → predicted id, distance, margin (or UNKNOWN).
- `gameplay eval` → confusion matrix, LOO accuracy, robustness report, recommended thresholds.

## Critical files / references reused

- Corpus + labels: `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/*.png` (+ `README.md` mapping).
- Screen catalog / canonical names: `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`.
- Conventions to mirror: `tools/marvin-perf/pyproject.toml`, `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/snapshot.py`
  (Pillow `Image.frombytes(... "BGR")` pattern), `tools/marvin-perf/tests/` layout.
- New journal template: structure of `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`.

## Docs / housekeeping (part of this slice)

- Create `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` (standard structure) seeded with: the location +
  host-only decisions, the analog-slop constraint, the Q10 fingerprint-method choice, and a
  phased plan (slice 1 = classifier; later = highlight reader, navigator, firmware export).
- Add the new journal to the list in `CLAUDE.md` and a pointer line in the auto-memory
  `MEMORY.md` (per the journal/subproject rules).
- Leave `gh3_navigation.md`'s "_(deferred to M9)_ classifier regions" item as-is; fill its
  vision section only once regions/thresholds settle (record findings in the new journal).

## Verification

From `tools/gameplay/` using the uv env (`UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache` in-sandbox):

- `uv run pytest` — all tests pass:
  - `test_screens`: every `gh3_screens/*.png` maps to a known id; id set matches nav-doc catalog.
  - `test_fingerprint`: deterministic; length `3·G·H`; values in `[0,255]`.
  - `test_classifier`: LOO accuracy ≥ bar (these screens are very distinct — expect ≥0.95);
    held-out-class → UNKNOWN.
  - `test_perturb`: classification stable across the slop envelope ≥ bar (e.g. ≥0.90).
- `uv run gameplay eval` — prints a clean confusion matrix, robustness report, recommended thresholds.
- Spot checks: `uv run gameplay classify firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/in_song__training.png`
  → `in_song`; same for a `song_select__bonus_*` (→ `song_select`) and a held-out-looking case.

## Out of scope (this slice)

Highlight/selection reader, number/score OCR, the navigator/controller, firmware
`gameplay_engine` port, and any firmware-facing template export.

```

ARM926EJ-S confirmed (SAM9X7 series, ARMv5TE single core, up to 800 MHz, no SIMD). That's enough — and crucially, this workload is **memory-bound, not compute-bound**, so the clock barely matters. Let me work the estimate and fold it into the plan.

The dominant cost is reading frame pixels from the uncached `.region_nocache` framebuffer. Compute (region sums + a 144-element L1 distance × 13 templates ≈ 1,900 byte ops) is microseconds — negligible. So the whole question is *how many pixels we touch*:

- **Dense** (every pixel): 720×480×3 ≈ 1.04 MB of uncached DDR reads. Uncached single-beat reads on the ARM926/MPDDRC run ~50–150 MB/s (no cache-line burst), so **~7–20 ms** per frame.
- **Subsampled** (sparse lattice per region, mirroring cv_marvin_v1's existing 5×5 patch sampling): ~48 regions × ~25 samples ≈ 1,200 reads → **well under 1 ms**.

Either way it's milliseconds, not seconds — and the observer only needs a few Hz for menu navigation. Subsampling is the obvious target (<1 ms, <1% CPU at 5–10 Hz) and is already the house pattern. ## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# GH3 game-state engine — offline prototype, slice 1: screen classifier

## Context

marvin needs a **game-state observer** (spec §4.8, milestone M9): watch the captured
video and recognize which GH3 screen the game is on (main_menu, song_select,
gameplay, pause, …), so the navigator (M10) can drive menus closed-loop along the
graph in [`gh3_navigation.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md). Per Q10 the
chosen approach is **fixed-region/color fingerprints**, not general CV — GH3's screens
and layouts are static.

The on-ramp work is done: `marvin-perf snapshot` has produced a labelled corpus of 102
real GH3 screens at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (720×480 PNG, 13 screen classes).
We prototype the detection algorithm **host-side in Python against that corpus first**,
prove it, and only later port the proven, simple logic to a firmware `gameplay_engine`
module (out of scope here).

**This slice = the screen classifier only** (not the highlight/selection reader, not the
navigator). Output for a frame: `screen_id` + confidence, or `UNKNOWN` (the navigator's
recovery path depends on a trustworthy UNKNOWN).

**Hard constraint — analog slop.** The Wii emits analog component video that is converted
to HDMI before capture, so any algorithm must tolerate (a) **positional slop** (overscan /
sub-pixel position drift, slight scale) and (b) **value slop** (gain/offset, limited↔full
range, analog noise). The corpus snapshots are *clean digital captures over the perf-log
path* and do **not** contain this slop, so robustness must be validated by injecting
synthetic perturbations. This is why the fingerprint is coarse region-averaged color, not
a pixel-exact template/hash.

**Decisions taken (this planning turn):** new `tools/gameplay/` subproject with its own uv
env + journal; host-only (no firmware-facing template export yet).

## Approach

Coarse **fixed-region mean-color fingerprint** + **nearest-centroid classifier** with an
**UNKNOWN reject** rule, plus an evaluation harness that includes a slop-robustness pass.
Everything is written to mirror cheap integer C (sum pixels per region, divide, L1
compare) so the eventual firmware port is mechanical — but no export is produced yet.

### New subproject layout: `tools/gameplay/`

Mirrors `tools/marvin-perf/` conventions (uv project, `pyproject.toml`, package + `tests/`).

```
tools/gameplay/
  pyproject.toml            # name="gameplay"; deps: pillow, numpy; dev: pytest; script: gameplay=gameplay.cli:main
  .python-version           # 3.12 (match marvin-perf)
  README.md
  docs/journal.md           # new subproject journal (CLAUDE.md rule 4)
  gameplay/
    __init__.py
    screens.py              # canonical ScreenId set + filename-prefix→id map (aligned with gh3_navigation.md)
    corpus.py               # locate gh3_screens/, load *.png → (screen_id, ndarray); derive label from filename prefix
    fingerprint.py          # region grid + fingerprint(img)->uint8 vector (integer per-region BGR means; C-shaped)
    classifier.py           # build_templates() centroids; classify(fp)->(id, dist, margin); UNKNOWN reject rule
    perturb.py              # synthetic analog-slop: brightness/gain/offset, translate, gaussian noise, scale/overscan crop
    evaluate.py             # LOO CV + confusion matrix + threshold sweep + robustness report
    cli.py                  # `gameplay classify <png>`, `gameplay eval`
  tests/{__init__,conftest,test_screens,test_fingerprint,test_classifier,test_perturb}.py
```

### `screens.py` — canonical ids + label map

13 ids matching the `gh3_navigation.md` catalog. The filename prefix (before `__`) maps to
the canonical id; two prefixes are renamed to match the nav doc:

- `difficulty` → `difficulty_select`
- `speed` → `speed_select`
- (all others map by identity: `main_menu`, `training_menu`, `tutorials_menu`,
  `song_select` — covers both `__NN_` and `__bonus_NN_` —, `part_select`,
  `section_select`, `loading`, `in_song`, `pause_menu`, `quit_confirm`, `practice_end_menu`)

This module is the single source of truth aligning prototype ids ↔ nav-doc screen names.

### `fingerprint.py` — the fixed-region signature (Q10)

- Resize input to a canonical 720×480 first (defensive against resolution drift).
- Partition into a coarse **G×H grid** (start **8×6 = 48 regions**; grid resolution is a
  swept parameter in eval). Each region → integer mean of (B,G,R). Fingerprint =
  concatenated `uint8` vector, length `3·G·H` (144 at 8×6).
- Coarse averaging is what buys positional-slop tolerance (sub-cell shifts wash out).
- **Sample density is a first-class knob** (see hardware-cost section): a region mean can
  be computed densely (every pixel) or from a sparse lattice of N samples per region
  (mirrors cv_marvin_v1's existing sparse 5×5 patch sampling). Eval measures accuracy at
  the *affordable* density so we prove the classifier at the pixel budget we'd spend on HW.
- Written as plain accumulate-sum-then-divide over rectangles so it ports 1:1 to integer C.
- Provide an optional per-frame **value-normalization** variant (e.g. subtract global mean
  luma / scale to fixed mean) to combat gain/offset slop; raw-vs-normalized is chosen
  **empirically in eval**, not assumed.

### `classifier.py` — nearest-centroid + UNKNOWN

- Template per class = **centroid** (mean fingerprint over that class's corpus samples).
  K small fixed-size templates (the future firmware metadata; not exported yet).
- `d_k = L1(fp, template_k)`; `best = argmin`, `second = next-smallest`.
- Accept `best` iff `d_best ≤ T_abs` **and** `(d_second − d_best) ≥ T_margin`; else UNKNOWN.
- Integer math throughout. Confidence derived from the margin.
- `song_select` is one class spanning main+bonus setlists; eval will reveal if the bonus
  tab variation hurts the centroid (treat as one class unless eval says otherwise).

### `evaluate.py` — prove it, including slop

1. **Leave-one-out CV** over multi-sample classes → accuracy + confusion matrix.
2. **Single-sample classes** (`loading`, `in_song`, `section_select`, `tutorials_menu`)
   can't LOO — report resubstitution + lean on the robustness pass; flag honestly.
3. **UNKNOWN-rejection test:** hold out an entire class's samples (centroid absent),
   confirm they reject as UNKNOWN — validates `T_abs`/`T_margin`.
4. **Slop-robustness pass (the analog point):** apply `perturb.py` transforms across an
   envelope (brightness/gain ±, offset, ±few-px translate, overscan crop/scale, noise σ)
   and report classification-stability rate + margin degradation per perturbation type.
5. **Threshold selection:** from the separation between in-class `d_best` and
   nearest-wrong-class distance, print recommended `T_abs`, `T_margin`.

### `cli.py`

- `gameplay classify <png>` → predicted id, distance, margin (or UNKNOWN).
- `gameplay eval` → confusion matrix, LOO accuracy, robustness report, recommended
  thresholds, **and estimated SAM9X75 time/classification at the chosen sample density**.

## Hardware cost on SAM9X75 (rough estimate)

The prototype is host Python, but the design must port to a cheap firmware
`gameplay_engine`. Target SoC: **ARM926EJ-S (ARMv5TE), single core, up to 800 MHz, no
SIMD**. This workload is **memory-bound, not compute-bound** — the CPU clock barely matters.

- **Dominant cost = reading frame pixels from uncached DDR.** The ISC framebuffer is in
  `.region_nocache` (journal 2026-05-20), so every pixel read is a full-DDR single-beat
  fetch with no cache-line burst — exactly the "full-frame scan would matter" case that
  entry flags. Uncached sequential read ≈ **50–150 MB/s**.
- **Compute is negligible:** per-region integer sums + a 144-dim L1 distance × 13 templates
  ≈ ~1,900 byte ops → microseconds.

Two implementation points on the accuracy/cost curve:

| Strategy | Pixels touched | Est. time / classification |
|---|---|---|
| **Dense** region means (every pixel) | 720×480×3 ≈ 1.04 MB | **~7–20 ms** (≈50–140 Hz equiv) |
| **Subsampled** lattice (~48 regions × ~25 samples) | ~1.2 K reads | **< 1 ms** |

Conclusion: even the dense worst case is **tens of milliseconds, nowhere near "seconds."**
The observer needs only a few Hz for menu nav, so the subsampled path (<1 ms, <1% CPU at
5–10 Hz) is the obvious target and matches the existing sparse-patch precedent. The eval
harness reports both accuracy **and** estimated on-device time at the chosen sample budget,
so we pick a density that is provably accurate *and* cheap before any firmware port.

## Critical files / references reused

- Corpus + labels: `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/*.png` (+ `README.md` mapping).
- Screen catalog / canonical names: `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`.
- Conventions to mirror: `tools/marvin-perf/pyproject.toml`, `tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/snapshot.py`
  (Pillow `Image.frombytes(... "BGR")` pattern), `tools/marvin-perf/tests/` layout.
- New journal template: structure of `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`.

## Docs / housekeeping (part of this slice)

- Create `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` (standard structure) seeded with: the location +
  host-only decisions, the analog-slop constraint, the Q10 fingerprint-method choice, and a
  phased plan (slice 1 = classifier; later = highlight reader, navigator, firmware export).
- Add the new journal to the list in `CLAUDE.md` and a pointer line in the auto-memory
  `MEMORY.md` (per the journal/subproject rules).
- Leave `gh3_navigation.md`'s "_(deferred to M9)_ classifier regions" item as-is; fill its
  vision section only once regions/thresholds settle (record findings in the new journal).

## Verification

From `tools/gameplay/` using the uv env (`UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache` in-sandbox):

- `uv run pytest` — all tests pass:
  - `test_screens`: every `gh3_screens/*.png` maps to a known id; id set matches nav-doc catalog.
  - `test_fingerprint`: deterministic; length `3·G·H`; values in `[0,255]`.
  - `test_classifier`: LOO accuracy ≥ bar (these screens are very distinct — expect ≥0.95);
    held-out-class → UNKNOWN.
  - `test_perturb`: classification stable across the slop envelope ≥ bar (e.g. ≥0.90).
- `uv run gameplay eval` — prints a clean confusion matrix, robustness report, recommended thresholds.
- Spot checks: `uv run gameplay classify firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/in_song__training.png`
  → `in_song`; same for a `song_select__bonus_*` (→ `song_select`) and a held-out-looking case.

## Out of scope (this slice)

Highlight/selection reader, number/score OCR, the navigator/controller, firmware
`gameplay_engine` port, and any firmware-facing template export.

```python
"""Canonical GH3 screen identifiers and the corpus filename -> id mapping.

Single source of truth aligning the prototype's screen ids with the screen names
in `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`. The classifier emits one of these ids
(or the sentinel UNKNOWN); the firmware `gameplay_engine` port will reuse the same
names.

Corpus files are named `<prefix>__<selection>.png` (or just `<prefix>.png` for
single-shot screens). The screen *class* is the prefix; the selection suffix is
the highlighted item, which a later slice (the highlight reader) handles. Two
prefixes are renamed here to match the nav-doc node names.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# Sentinel for "no recognized screen" — the navigator's recovery path keys off it.
UNKNOWN = "unknown"

# Canonical screen ids, matching the gh3_navigation.md catalog. Order is the
# nominal practice-run flow, then the overlays/dialogs.
SCREEN_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "main_menu",
    "training_menu",
    "tutorials_menu",
    "song_select",
    "part_select",
    "difficulty_select",
    "section_select",
    "speed_select",
    "loading",
    "in_song",
    "pause_menu",
    "quit_confirm",
    "practice_end_menu",
)

# Corpus filename prefixes whose canonical id differs from the prefix itself.
# Everything else maps by identity.
_PREFIX_RENAMES: dict[str, str] = {
    "difficulty": "difficulty_select",
    "speed": "speed_select",
}


def screen_id_for_filename(filename: str) -> str:
    """Map a corpus PNG filename to its canonical screen id.

    `main_menu__training.png` -> `main_menu`; `difficulty__hard.png` ->
    `difficulty_select`; `loading.png` -> `loading`. Raises ValueError if the
    resulting id isn't a known screen.
    """
    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    if stem.endswith(".png"):
        stem = stem[: -len(".png")]
    prefix = stem.split("__", 1)[0]
    screen_id = _PREFIX_RENAMES.get(prefix, prefix)
    if screen_id not in SCREEN_IDS:
        raise ValueError(f"{filename!r}: unknown screen prefix {prefix!r}")
    return screen_id

```

```python
"""Load the labelled GH3 screen corpus.

The corpus is the renamed snapshot set at `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/`
(720x480 PNGs). Each image's screen-class label comes from its filename via
`screens.screen_id_for_filename`. Images are returned as uint8 HxWx3 arrays in
**BGR** order, matching marvin's native framebuffer layout (capture is BGR888
packed; see marvin journal 2026-05-02).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

from .screens import screen_id_for_filename

# tools/gameplay/gameplay/corpus.py -> repo root is parents[3].
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
_DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "firmware" / "marvin" / "docs" / "gh3_screens"


def corpus_dir() -> Path:
    """Resolve the corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR)."""
    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR")
    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Sample:
    screen_id: str
    path: Path
    image: np.ndarray  # uint8, HxWx3, BGR


def load_bgr(path: str | Path) -> np.ndarray:
    """Load an image file as a uint8 HxWx3 BGR array."""
    with Image.open(path) as im:
        rgb = np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"), dtype=np.uint8)
    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR


def load_corpus(directory: str | Path | None = None) -> list[Sample]:
    """Load every `*.png` in the corpus directory as labelled `Sample`s.

    Sorted by filename for determinism. Raises FileNotFoundError if the
    directory is empty or missing.
    """
    d = Path(directory) if directory is not None else corpus_dir()
    files = sorted(d.glob("*.png"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no PNGs found in corpus dir {d}")
    return [
        Sample(screen_id=screen_id_for_filename(f.name), path=f, image=load_bgr(f))
        for f in files
    ]

```

"""Fixed-region colour fingerprint (the Q10 recognizer primitive).

A frame is partitioned into a coarse `cols x rows` grid of fixed rectangles; each
region collapses to its mean (B,G,R). The fingerprint is the concatenated uint8
vector, length `3 * cols * rows`. Coarse averaging is what makes this tolerant of
the positional slop introduced by the Wii's analog-component -> HDMI path: a
sub-cell shift just moves a few pixels between neighbours and washes out.

Two knobs matter for the firmware port (memory-bound on uncached DDR reads — see
the plan's hardware-cost section):

- `samples_per_region`: None computes a dense mean (touches every pixel ~= a
  full-frame scan, ~7-20 ms on the SAM9X75). An integer N samples an N x N lattice
  per region instead (~cols*rows*N*N reads total, sub-millisecond), trading a little
  estimate noise for speed. The coarse average absorbs that noise.
- `normalize`: when True, the vector is standardized to a fixed mean/std per frame,
  which cancels the global gain/offset value-slop of the analog path. Raw vs
  normalized is chosen empirically in `evaluate.py`.

Everything is shaped to port 1:1 to integer C: accumulate pixel sums over fixed
rectangles (or fixed sample coords), divide, then an L1 compare downstream.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

CANONICAL_W = 720
CANONICAL_H = 480
BPP = 3  # BGR

# Standardization targets for the normalized variant (uint8 midpoint-ish).
_NORM_MEAN = 128.0
_NORM_STD = 48.0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FingerprintConfig:
    cols: int = 8
    rows: int = 6
    samples_per_region: int | None = 5  # None = dense; N = N x N lattice
    normalize: bool = False

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return self.cols * self.rows * BPP

    @property
    def pixel_reads(self) -> int:
        """Pixels touched per classification — the on-device cost driver."""
        if self.samples_per_region is None:
            return CANONICAL_W * CANONICAL_H
        return self.cols * self.rows * self.samples_per_region**2


DEFAULT_CONFIG = FingerprintConfig()


def _to_canonical(image: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Ensure a uint8 HxWx3 array at the canonical 720x480 (resize if needed)."""
    if image.dtype != np.uint8:
        image = image.astype(np.uint8)
    if image.shape[:2] == (CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W):
        return image
    # Defensive only — real captures are already native 720x480. Resize via PIL
    # (BGR in, BGR out; channel order is irrelevant to a resize).
    im = Image.fromarray(image, mode="RGB")
    im = im.resize((CANONICAL_W, CANONICAL_H), Image.BILINEAR)
    return np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)


def _region_bounds(n: int, extent: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Split [0, extent) into n contiguous integer spans."""
    edges = np.linspace(0, extent, n + 1).round().astype(int)
    return [(int(edges[i]), int(edges[i + 1])) for i in range(n)]


def _lattice(lo: int, hi: int, n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """n sample coordinates inside [lo, hi), centred in their sub-cells."""
    fracs = (np.arange(n) + 0.5) / n
    return (lo + fracs * (hi - lo)).astype(int).clip(lo, hi - 1)


def fingerprint(image: np.ndarray, config: FingerprintConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute the fixed-region fingerprint of a BGR frame.

    Returns a uint8 vector of length `config.length`, region-major (row 0 first),
    each region contributing [B, G, R].
    """
    img = _to_canonical(image)
    ys = _region_bounds(config.rows, CANONICAL_H)
    xs = _region_bounds(config.cols, CANONICAL_W)

    means = np.empty((config.rows, config.cols, BPP), dtype=np.float64)
    for r, (y0, y1) in enumerate(ys):
        for c, (x0, x1) in enumerate(xs):
            if config.samples_per_region is None:
                patch = img[y0:y1, x0:x1, :]
            else:
                yy = _lattice(y0, y1, config.samples_per_region)
                xx = _lattice(x0, x1, config.samples_per_region)
                patch = img[np.ix_(yy, xx)]
            means[r, c] = patch.reshape(-1, BPP).mean(axis=0)

    vec = means.reshape(-1)
    if config.normalize:
        std = vec.std()
        if std > 1e-6:
            vec = (vec - vec.mean()) / std * _NORM_STD + _NORM_MEAN
        else:
            vec = np.full_like(vec, _NORM_MEAN)
    return vec.round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

```python
"""Nearest-centroid screen classifier with an UNKNOWN reject rule.

Each screen class is represented by one centroid fingerprint (the mean over its
corpus samples) — a small fixed-size template, which is the per-state metadata the
firmware `gameplay_engine` will eventually carry. Classification is L1 distance to
every centroid, argmin, then a two-part accept test:

    accept best iff  d_best <= t_abs  AND  (d_second - d_best) >= t_margin

Otherwise the result is UNKNOWN. The navigator's recovery path depends on a
trustworthy UNKNOWN, so the margin gate (am I *clearly* closer to one class than the
next?) matters as much as the absolute gate. All math is integer L1 over uint8
vectors, matching the firmware target.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from .fingerprint import FingerprintConfig, fingerprint
from .screens import UNKNOWN

# Defaults; `evaluate.py` recommends concrete values from the corpus separation.
DEFAULT_T_ABS = 4000
DEFAULT_T_MARGIN = 400


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Templates:
    ids: tuple[str, ...]
    centroids: np.ndarray  # (K, L) uint8
    config: FingerprintConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Classification:
    screen_id: str  # a canonical id, or UNKNOWN
    best_id: str  # nearest centroid regardless of reject (for diagnostics)
    best_dist: int
    second_dist: int

    @property
    def margin(self) -> int:
        return self.second_dist - self.best_dist

    @property
    def accepted(self) -> bool:
        return self.screen_id != UNKNOWN


def build_templates(
    labelled_fps: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]], config: FingerprintConfig
) -> Templates:
    """Build per-class centroids from labelled fingerprints (id -> [fp, ...])."""
    ids = tuple(sorted(labelled_fps))
    centroids = np.empty((len(ids), config.length), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i, sid in enumerate(ids):
        stack = np.stack(labelled_fps[sid]).astype(np.float64)
        centroids[i] = stack.mean(axis=0).round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return Templates(ids=ids, centroids=centroids, config=config)


def _l1_to_centroids(fp: np.ndarray, centroids: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    diff = centroids.astype(np.int32) - fp.astype(np.int32)
    return np.abs(diff).sum(axis=1)


def classify_fp(
    fp: np.ndarray,
    templates: Templates,
    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
) -> Classification:
    """Classify a precomputed fingerprint against templates."""
    dists = _l1_to_centroids(fp, templates.centroids)
    order = np.argsort(dists, kind="stable")
    best_i = int(order[0])
    best_d = int(dists[best_i])
    second_d = int(dists[order[1]]) if len(order) > 1 else (best_d + t_margin)
    best_id = templates.ids[best_i]

    accept = best_d <= t_abs and (second_d - best_d) >= t_margin
    return Classification(
        screen_id=best_id if accept else UNKNOWN,
        best_id=best_id,
        best_dist=best_d,
        second_dist=second_d,
    )


def classify_image(
    image: np.ndarray,
    templates: Templates,
    t_abs: int = DEFAULT_T_ABS,
    t_margin: int = DEFAULT_T_MARGIN,
) -> Classification:
    """Classify a raw BGR frame (fingerprints it with the templates' config)."""
    fp = fingerprint(image, templates.config)
    return classify_fp(fp, templates, t_abs=t_abs, t_margin=t_margin)

```python
"""Synthetic analog-slop perturbations for robustness testing.

The corpus snapshots are clean digital captures over the perf-log path, so they
lack the distortions the real Wii feed has: it is analog component video converted
to HDMI before capture. To test whether the classifier survives that, we inject
the two slop families it introduces:

- **value slop** — gain (brightness scaling), offset, sensor/analog noise;
- **positional slop** — sub-cell translation, slight scale (overscan in/out).

Transforms operate on uint8 HxWx3 BGR arrays and are deterministic given an rng.
`envelope()` yields a fixed, named battery used by `evaluate.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image


def adjust_gain(img: np.ndarray, gain: float) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) * gain, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def adjust_offset(img: np.ndarray, offset: float) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + offset, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def add_noise(img: np.ndarray, sigma: float, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    noise = rng.normal(0.0, sigma, size=img.shape)
    return np.clip(img.astype(np.float32) + noise, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def translate(img: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Shift by (dx, dy) px, filling exposed edges by replication."""
    h, w = img.shape[:2]
    padded = np.pad(img, ((abs(dy), abs(dy)), (abs(dx), abs(dx)), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
    y0, x0 = abs(dy) - dy, abs(dx) - dx
    return padded[y0 : y0 + h, x0 : x0 + w]


def rescale(img: np.ndarray, factor: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zoom about the centre by `factor`, then centre-crop/pad back to the
    original size (factor>1 = overscan crop, factor<1 = borders appear)."""
    h, w = img.shape[:2]
    nw, nh = max(1, round(w * factor)), max(1, round(h * factor))
    im = Image.fromarray(img, mode="RGB").resize((nw, nh), Image.BILINEAR)
    scaled = np.asarray(im, dtype=np.uint8)

    out = np.empty_like(img)
    # x axis
    if nw >= w:
        sx = (nw - w) // 2
        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = sx, 0, w
    else:
        dx = (w - nw) // 2
        xs_src, xs_dst, cw = 0, dx, nw
    if nh >= h:
        sy = (nh - h) // 2
        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = sy, 0, h
    else:
        dy = (h - nh) // 2
        ys_src, ys_dst, ch = 0, dy, nh

    if nw < w or nh < h:  # borders exposed — fill by edge replication
        edge = np.pad(scaled, ((0, 0), (0, 0), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
        out[:] = np.pad(
            edge,
            ((ys_dst, h - ys_dst - ch), (xs_dst, w - xs_dst - cw), (0, 0)),
            mode="edge",
        )
    else:
        out[ys_dst : ys_dst + ch, xs_dst : xs_dst + cw] = scaled[
            ys_src : ys_src + ch, xs_src : xs_src + cw
        ]
    return out


def envelope(img: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Yield (category, name, perturbed_image) over a fixed slop battery."""
    yield "gain", "gain-0.85", adjust_gain(img, 0.85)
    yield "gain", "gain-1.15", adjust_gain(img, 1.15)
    yield "offset", "offset-neg20", adjust_offset(img, -20)
    yield "offset", "offset-pos20", adjust_offset(img, 20)
    yield "noise", "noise-sigma6", add_noise(img, 6.0, rng)
    yield "noise", "noise-sigma12", add_noise(img, 12.0, rng)
    yield "translate", "shift-x4", translate(img, 4, 0)
    yield "translate", "shift-y4", translate(img, 0, 4)
    yield "translate", "shift-xy6", translate(img, -6, 6)
    yield "scale", "overscan-1.03", rescale(img, 1.03)
    yield "scale", "underscan-0.97", rescale(img, 0.97)
