```text
258	
259	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
260	                                 int x, int y,
261	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
262	{
263	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
264	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
265	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
266	}
267	
268	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
269	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
270	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
271	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
272	{
273	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
274	    while (x >= y)
275	    {
276	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
277	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
278	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
279	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
280	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
281	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
282	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
283	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
284	        y++;
285	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
286	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
287	    }
288	}
289	
290	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
291	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
292	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
293	{
294	    int rr = radius * radius;
295	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
296	    {
297	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
298	        {
299	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
300	            {
301	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
302	            }
303	        }
304	    }
305	}

307	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching

310	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
311	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
312	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */

317	 * outside the buffer are clipped by put_pixel_bgr. */
318	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t bw, uint16_t bh,
319	                         uint16_t ox, uint16_t oy)
320	{
321	    int w = (int)bw, h = (int)bh;
322	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
323	    {
324	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
325	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
326	        int hx = (int)s.hx - (int)ox, hy = (int)s.hy - (int)oy;
327	        int ex = (int)s.ex - (int)ox, ey = (int)s.ey - (int)oy;
328	
329	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
330	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
331	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
332	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
333	
334	        if (s_pressed[i])
335	        {
336	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
337	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
338	        }
339	        if (s_edge_active[i])
340	        {
341	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
342	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
343	        }
344	    }
345	}
346	
347	/* ─── Detector-config publish ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
348	
349	/* Snapshot the static cv_marvin_v1 tables (sample coords, thresholds,
350	 * color filter weights) into a wire record. Static today; when M6
351	 * calibration UI lands and these become runtime-tunable, this function
352	 * is the single point that re-publishes after each tweak. */
353	static void publish_detector_config(void)
354	{
355	    perf_rec_detector_config_t cfg;
356	    memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
357	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
358	    {
359	        cfg.sensor_hx[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hx;
360	        cfg.sensor_hy[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hy;
361	        cfg.sensor_ex[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ex;
362	        cfg.sensor_ey[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ey;
363	        cfg.color_target_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[0];
364	        cfg.color_target_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[1];
365	        cfg.color_target_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[2];
366	        cfg.color_reject_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[0];
367	        cfg.color_reject_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[1];
368	        cfg.color_reject_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[2];
369	    }
370	    cfg.hold_thresh       = CV_HOLD_THRESH;
371	    cfg.hold_release_frac = CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
372	    cfg.edge_thresh       = CV_EDGE_THRESH;
373	    PerfLog_EmitDetectorConfig(&cfg);
374	}
375	
376	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
377	
378	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
379	{
380	    (void)param;
381	
382	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
383	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
384	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
385	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
386	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
387	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
388	    configASSERT(subscribed);
389	
390	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
391	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
392	
393	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
394	
395	    publish_detector_config();
396	
397	    for (;;)
398	    {
399	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
400	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
401	
402	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
403	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
404	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
405	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
406	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
407	
408	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
409	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
410	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
411	
412	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
413	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
414	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
415	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
416	         * directly from the setter path. */
417	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
418	
419	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
420	
421	        /* STRIKE: the strum trigger zone, copied straight from the frame (no
422	         * sensors there → no rings). */
423	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
424	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
425	                                   CV_STRIKE_X, CV_STRIKE_Y, CV_STRIKE_W, CV_STRIKE_H);
426	
427	        /* SENSING: copy the sensor row into scratch and (when the overlay sink
428	         * is on) paint the target rings onto the copy before shipping it. The
429	         * source frame is never written, so snapshots and the LVDS panel stay
430	         * clean. Gate the copy on the STRIP mask so it costs nothing when the
431	         * host isn't consuming strips. */
432	        if ((PerfLog_GetEnabledMask() & (1u << PERF_REC_STRIP)) != 0u)
433	        {
434	            const uint8_t *src = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer
435	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_Y * fstride
436	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_X * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
437	            const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_W * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
438	            uint8_t *dst = s_sensing_scratch;
439	            for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < CV_SENSING_H; row++)
440	            {
441	                memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
442	                src += fstride;
443	                dst += row_bytes;
444	            }
445	            if ((PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags() & PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP) != 0u)
446	            {
447	                draw_overlay(s_sensing_scratch, CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H,
448	                             CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y);
449	            }
450	            PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
451	                                    CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y,
452	                                    CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H, s_sensing_scratch);
453	        }
454	
455	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
456	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
457	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)
458	        // {
459	        //     LOG_INFO("CV: G %3d/%3d%c%c R %3d/%3d%c%c Y %3d/%3d%c%c B %3d/%3d%c%c O %3d/%3d%c%c\r\n",
460	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_GREEN],  (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_GREEN],
461	        //              s_pressed[FRET_GREEN]      ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_GREEN]  ? 'E' : '.',
462	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_RED],    (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_RED],
463	        //              s_pressed[FRET_RED]        ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_RED]    ? 'E' : '.',
464	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_YELLOW], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_YELLOW],
465	        //              s_pressed[FRET_YELLOW]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_YELLOW] ? 'E' : '.',
466	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_BLUE],   (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_BLUE],
467	        //              s_pressed[FRET_BLUE]       ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_BLUE]   ? 'E' : '.',
468	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_ORANGE], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_ORANGE],
469	        //              s_pressed[FRET_ORANGE]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_ORANGE] ? 'E' : '.');
470	        // }
471	    }
```

```h
#ifndef GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H
#define GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "queue.h"

/* Game-state observer — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.8 (M9).
 *
 * A video-frame consumer (not a detector): it classifies which GH3 screen the
 * captured frame shows and publishes typed game_state_t events on its own bus
 * (xGameStateQueue), kept separate from the detector-state bus per the §4.2
 * multi-detector decision. The recognizer data (region grid, per-class
 * centroids, thresholds) is the host-proven metadata frozen into
 * game/gameplay_metadata.h by `gameplay export-c`.
 *
 * Phase 1 (this module): screen classification only. Selection/song readers
 * (Phase 2) and the navigator/controller (Phase 3, M10) build on this. */

typedef struct
{
    uint32_t frame_epoch;   /* master sync token, = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count */
    uint64_t timestamp_us;  /* monotonic, marvin-local */
    uint8_t  screen;        /* GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN */
    uint8_t  reserved[3];
    int32_t  best_dist;     /* L1 to the nearest centroid */
    int32_t  margin;        /* second-best − best (confidence) */
} game_state_t;

/* Brings up the game-state bus queue and the observer task. The observer
 * subscribes to the video frame queue from inside its task, so call this after
 * Video_Initialize. Observation starts disabled; call SetObserveEnabled(true)
 * to begin publishing (spec §6 game_observe_enable). */
void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void);

/* Game-state event bus. Consumers (operator UI, the controller at M10) read
 * here. Returns NULL until GameplayEngine_Initialize has run. */
QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void);

/* Observation toggle. When off the task still drains frames (so the video
 * queue doesn't back up) but classifies nothing and emits no events. */
void GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(bool on);
bool GameplayEngine_ObserveEnabled(void);

/* Most recently classified screen (GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN);
 * GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN before the first classified frame. */
uint8_t GameplayEngine_CurrentScreen(void);

#endif
```

```h
/* Pure screen-classification math, ported from the host prototype
 * (tools/gameplay) and driven by the generated game/gameplay_metadata.h tables.
 * Deliberately free of FreeRTOS / video dependencies so it compiles and can be
 * numerically cross-checked against the Python classifier on a host, then links
 * unchanged into the firmware game_task (gameplay_engine.c). Not reentrant — it
 * uses a static fingerprint scratch; only the single observer task calls it. */

/* Classify a BGR888 frame (3 B/pixel, width*height). Returns a GP_SCREEN_*
 * index (see gameplay_metadata.h) or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN. The frame must be at the
 * canonical GP_CANON_W × GP_CANON_H (no resize on-target — the Wii is 720×480);
 * any other size returns GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN. When non-NULL, *out_best_dist and
 * *out_margin receive the nearest-centroid L1 distance and the second-best−best
 * margin. */
uint8_t gp_classify(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
                    int32_t *out_best_dist, int32_t *out_margin);

/* Compute the raw fingerprint (GP_FP_LEN uint8 values) for a canonical frame,
 * without classifying — exposed for the host cross-validation test. Returns 0
 * on success, non-zero if the frame isn't the canonical size. */
int gp_fingerprint(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, uint8_t *out);

#endif
```

```c
#include "game/gameplay_classify.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Per-frame value normalization targets — must match the host prototype
 * (tools/gameplay/gameplay/fingerprint.py: _NORM_MEAN / _NORM_STD). */
#define GP_NORM_MEAN  128.0f
#define GP_NORM_STD   48.0f
#define GP_BPP        3

/* Split [0, extent) into `n` contiguous spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
{
    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
}

/* j-th of `n` sample coordinates centred in their sub-cell of [lo, hi). */
static int gp_lattice(int j, int lo, int hi, int n)
{
    int c = (int)((double)lo + (((double)j + 0.5) / (double)n) * (double)(hi - lo));
    if (c < lo)      { c = lo; }
    if (c > hi - 1)  { c = hi - 1; }
    return c;
}

/* Mean BGR over the GP_FP_SAMPLES × GP_FP_SAMPLES lattice of a region. */
static void gp_region_mean(const uint8_t *frame, int w,
                           int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
{
    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u;
    int n = GP_FP_SAMPLES;
    for (int jy = 0; jy < n; jy++)
    {
        int y = gp_lattice(jy, y0, y1, n);
        const uint8_t *row = frame + (uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w * GP_BPP;
        for (int jx = 0; jx < n; jx++)
        {
            int x = gp_lattice(jx, x0, x1, n);
            const uint8_t *p = row + (uint32_t)x * GP_BPP;
            sb += p[0];
            sg += p[1];
            sr += p[2];
        }
    }
    float cnt = (float)(n * n);
    out[0] = (float)sb / cnt;
    out[1] = (float)sg / cnt;
    out[2] = (float)sr / cnt;
}

/* Fingerprint scratch in normalized float space, reduced to uint8. Static — the
 * single observer task is the only caller (see header). */
static float s_fp_f[GP_FP_LEN];

int gp_fingerprint(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, uint8_t *out)
{
    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }

    int idx = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < GP_FP_ROWS; r++)
    {
        int y0 = gp_edge(r, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
        int y1 = gp_edge(r + 1, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
        for (int c = 0; c < GP_FP_COLS; c++)
        {
            int x0 = gp_edge(c, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
            int x1 = gp_edge(c + 1, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
            float bgr[3];
            gp_region_mean(frame, width, x0, y0, x1, y1, bgr);
            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[0];
            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[1];
            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[2];
        }
    }

#if GP_FP_NORMALIZE
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++) { sum += s_fp_f[i]; }
    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)GP_FP_LEN);
    double var = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
    {
        double d = (double)s_fp_f[i] - (double)mean;
        var += d * d;
    }
    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)GP_FP_LEN);
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
    {
        float v = (std > 1e-6f)
                ? ((s_fp_f[i] - mean) / std * GP_NORM_STD + GP_NORM_MEAN)
                : GP_NORM_MEAN;
        long q = lroundf(v);
        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
    }
#else
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
    {
        long q = lroundf(s_fp_f[i]);
        if (q < 0)        { q = 0; }
        else if (q > 255) { q = 255; }
        out[i] = (uint8_t)q;
    }
#endif
    return 0;
}

static uint8_t s_fp[GP_FP_LEN];

uint8_t gp_classify(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
                    int32_t *out_best_dist, int32_t *out_margin)
{
    if (gp_fingerprint(frame, width, height, s_fp) != 0)
    {
        if (out_best_dist) { *out_best_dist = INT32_MAX; }
        if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = 0; }
        return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
    }

    int32_t best = INT32_MAX, second = INT32_MAX;
    int best_k = -1;
    for (int k = 0; k < GP_N_SCREENS; k++)
    {
        const uint8_t *cen = gp_centroids[k];
        int32_t d = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++)
        {
            int diff = (int)s_fp[i] - (int)cen[i];
            d += (diff < 0) ? -diff : diff;
        }
        if (d < best)        { second = best; best = d; best_k = k; }
        else if (d < second) { second = d; }
    }

    int32_t margin = second - best;
    if (out_best_dist) { *out_best_dist = best; }
    if (out_margin)    { *out_margin = margin; }

    if (best <= GP_CLS_T_ABS && margin >= GP_CLS_T_MARGIN)
    {
        return (uint8_t)best_k;
    }
    return GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
}

```

```c
#include "game/gameplay_engine.h"
#include "game/gameplay_classify.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "queue.h"

#include "log.h"
#include "video/video.h"

#define GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS   1024u
#define GAME_TASK_PRIORITY      4u    /* vision tier (peer of cv_marvin_v1) */
#define GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH  1u    /* newest-frame-only */
#define GAME_BUS_DEPTH          8u
#define GAME_BYTES_PER_PIXEL    3u
#define GAME_US_PER_TICK        (1000000u / configTICK_RATE_HZ)

static QueueHandle_t s_bus_queue;
static StaticQueue_t s_bus_queue_buf;
static uint8_t       s_bus_queue_storage[GAME_BUS_DEPTH * sizeof(game_state_t)];

static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];

static StackType_t   s_task_stack[GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

static volatile bool    s_observe_enabled;
static volatile uint8_t s_current_screen = GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;

static const char *screen_name(uint8_t idx)
{
    return (idx < GP_N_SCREENS) ? gp_screen_ids[idx] : "unknown";
}

static void game_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
    configASSERT(subscribed);

    LOG_INFO("GAME: gameplay_engine started\r\n");

    uint8_t last_emitted = GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;

    for (;;)
    {
        Video_FrameInfo frame;
        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }

        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
        if (!s_observe_enabled)                            { continue; }
        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                          { continue; }
        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != GAME_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) { continue; }

        int32_t best_dist = 0, margin = 0;
        uint8_t screen = gp_classify((const uint8_t *)frame.buffer,
                                     (int)frame.width, (int)frame.height,
                                     &best_dist, &margin);
        s_current_screen = screen;

        /* Event semantics: publish (and log) only on a screen change. */
        if (screen != last_emitted)
        {
            game_state_t ev;
            memset(&ev, 0, sizeof(ev));
            ev.frame_epoch  = frame.frame_count;
            ev.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * GAME_US_PER_TICK;
            ev.screen       = screen;
            ev.best_dist    = best_dist;
            ev.margin       = margin;
            (void)xQueueSend(s_bus_queue, &ev, 0);

            LOG_INFO("GAME: screen %s (dist=%ld margin=%ld)\r\n",
                     screen_name(screen), (long)best_dist, (long)margin);
            last_emitted = screen;
        }
    }
}

void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void)
{
    s_bus_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_BUS_DEPTH,
                                     sizeof(game_state_t),
                                     s_bus_queue_storage,
                                     &s_bus_queue_buf);
    configASSERT(s_bus_queue != NULL);

    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(game_task, "GameEngine", GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL, GAME_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
}

QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void)
{
    return s_bus_queue;
}

void GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(bool on)
{
    s_observe_enabled = on;
}

bool GameplayEngine_ObserveEnabled(void)
{
    return s_observe_enabled;
}

uint8_t GameplayEngine_CurrentScreen(void)
{
    return s_current_screen;
}

```

```python
"""Cross-validate the firmware C classifier against the Python prototype.

The marvin port can't be built here (MPLAB/XC32 on Greg's side), but the *pure*
classification math lives in a FreeRTOS-free unit
(`firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_classify.c`) driven by the generated
`gameplay_metadata.h`. This test compiles that unit with `cc` into a tiny driver,
runs it on raw BGR dumps of real corpus frames, and asserts the C screen
decision matches `classify_image` from the prototype — proving the port (and the
exported metadata) reproduce the proven algorithm before it ever hits hardware.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from gameplay.classifier import build_templates, classify_image
from gameplay.evaluate import labelled_fps, recommend_thresholds
from gameplay.export_c import build_metadata_header
from gameplay.fingerprint import CANONICAL_H, CANONICAL_W, FingerprintConfig
from gameplay.screens import UNKNOWN

_REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
_FW_SRC = _REPO / "firmware" / "marvin" / "default" / "src"
_UNKNOWN_IDX = 255

_DRIVER_C = r"""
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "game/gameplay_classify.h"
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 4) return 2;
    int w = atoi(argv[2]), h = atoi(argv[3]);
    long n = (long)w * h * 3;
    unsigned char *buf = malloc((size_t)n);
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!f || fread(buf, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) return 3;
    fclose(f);
    int32_t bd = 0, mg = 0;
    uint8_t s = gp_classify(buf, w, h, &bd, &mg);
    printf("%d\n", (int)s);
    return 0;
}
"""

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("cc") is None, reason="no C compiler")


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def driver(tmp_path_factory):
    d = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("fwcls")
    # Use the same generated header the firmware compiles in.
    (_FW_SRC / "game" / "gameplay_metadata.h").write_text(
        build_metadata_header()
    ) if not (_FW_SRC / "game" / "gameplay_metadata.h").exists() else None
    (d / "driver.c").write_text(_DRIVER_C)
    exe = d / "driver"
    r = subprocess.run(
        ["cc", "-I", str(_FW_SRC), "-std=c11", "-O1",
         str(d / "driver.c"), str(_FW_SRC / "game" / "gameplay_classify.c"),
         "-lm", "-o", str(exe)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    return exe


def _c_classify(exe: Path, image, tmp: Path) -> int:
    raw = tmp / "frame.bgr"
    raw.write_bytes(image.tobytes())
    out = subprocess.run(
        [str(exe), str(raw), str(CANONICAL_W), str(CANONICAL_H)],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    return int(out.stdout.strip())


def test_c_matches_python_on_corpus(corpus, driver, tmp_path):
    cfg = FingerprintConfig()
    templates = build_templates(labelled_fps(corpus, cfg), cfg)
    rec = recommend_thresholds(corpus, cfg)
    ids = list(templates.ids)

    # One frame per screen class + a few song_select variants (subprocess per frame).
    seen: set[str] = set()
    sample = []
    for s in corpus:
        if s.screen_id not in seen:
            seen.add(s.screen_id)
            sample.append(s)
    sample += [s for s in corpus if s.screen_id == "song_select"][:5]

    for s in sample:
        py = classify_image(s.image, templates, t_abs=rec.rec_t_abs, t_margin=rec.rec_t_margin)
        py_idx = _UNKNOWN_IDX if py.screen_id == UNKNOWN else ids.index(py.screen_id)
        c_idx = _c_classify(driver, s.image, tmp_path)
        assert c_idx == py_idx, f"{s.path.name}: C={c_idx} Python={py_idx}"
```

Phase 1 — the M9 screen-classifier observer — is code-complete and validated as far as I can without MPLAB.

## What landed (firmware `game/` module, no MCC regen)

- **`gameplay_metadata.h`** — generated by `gameplay export-c` (region grid, `uint8` centroids, thresholds, screen-id table).
- **`gameplay_classify.{h,c}`** — the pure classify math (fixed-region fingerprint → per-frame normalize → L1-to-centroids → margin/abs reject), deliberately **FreeRTOS-free** so it's host-compilable.
- **`gameplay_engine.{h,c}`** — the `game_task`: subscribes to the video frame queue like `cv_marvin_v1`, classifies each 720×480 frame, and publishes `game_state_t` on a new `xGameStateQueue` on screen change (+ a `LOG_INFO`).
- Wired into `app.c` (`GameplayEngine_Initialize` + `SetObserveEnabled(true)`) and `user.cmake`.

## Validated without hardware

Since you build in MPLAB, I leaned on two host checks:
1. The pure unit **compiles clean** under `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`.
2. A new cross-validation test compiles `gameplay_classify.c` into a driver and confirms its screen decision **matches the Python `classify_image` on real corpus frames** — so the C port *and* the exported metadata reproduce the proven algorithm numerically. (49 tests green.)

The structural split (pure math vs FreeRTOS task) is what made that cross-check possible, and it's reusable for Phases 2–3.

## Status & caveats

**Code-complete + syntax-checked; not yet built in MPLAB or run on hardware** — that's your half of the loop. When you build, the first thing to watch is the `GameEngine` task's stack/heap and that it coexists with `cv_marvin_v1` as a second frame subscriber (both vision-tier prio 4, within the 4-subscriber cap).

```h
#ifndef GAMEPLAY_SELECT_H
#define GAMEPLAY_SELECT_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

/* Selection readers, ported from the host prototype (tools/gameplay) and driven
 * by game/gameplay_metadata.h. Pure (no FreeRTOS/video), so they compile and
 * cross-check on a host before linking into the observer task. Not reentrant
 * (static scratch); only the single observer task calls them. */

/* The static-list menu layout for a screen (GP_SCREEN_* index), or NULL if that
 * screen isn't a modelled static list. */
const gp_menu_layout_t *gp_menu_for_screen(uint8_t screen);

/* Static-list highlight: which cell/item is selected on `menu` for a canonical
 * BGR frame — the cell that deviates most from its learned unselected baseline.
 * Returns the cell index [0, menu->count), or -1 on a bad frame size. */
int gp_read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
                      const gp_menu_layout_t *menu);

typedef struct
{
    uint8_t setlist;  /* GP_SETLIST_MAIN | GP_SETLIST_BONUS */
    uint8_t index;    /* song ordinal within its setlist */
    int16_t tmpl;     /* index into gp_song_templates, or -1 */
} gp_song_t;

/* song_select: identify the selected song by nearest-template bitmap match
 * (offset search across both setlists). Fills *out; returns 0 on success, -1 on
 * a bad frame size. */
int gp_read_song(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, gp_song_t *out);

#endif

```

```c
#include "game/gameplay_select.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define GP_BPP            3
#define GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS  16   /* >= max items on any modelled menu (7) */

/* Split [0, extent) into `n` spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
{
    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
}

const gp_menu_layout_t *gp_menu_for_screen(uint8_t screen)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_N_MENUS; i++)
    {
        if (gp_menus[i].screen == screen) { return &gp_menus[i]; }
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* Mean BGR over [x0,x1)×[y0,y1), clamped to the frame. */
static void gp_rect_mean_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
                             int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
{
    if (x0 < 0) { x0 = 0; }  if (x1 > w) { x1 = w; }
    if (y0 < 0) { y0 = 0; }  if (y1 > h) { y1 = h; }
    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u, n = 0u;
    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
    {
        const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)x0) * GP_BPP;
        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
        {
            sb += p[0]; sg += p[1]; sr += p[2];
            p += GP_BPP;
            n++;
        }
    }
    if (n == 0u) { out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = 0.0f; return; }
    out[0] = (float)sb / (float)n;
    out[1] = (float)sg / (float)n;
    out[2] = (float)sr / (float)n;
}

int gp_read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
                      const gp_menu_layout_t *menu)
{
    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H) { return -1; }
    int count = menu->count;
    if (count > GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS) { count = GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS; }

    float col[GP_SEL_MAX_CELLS][3];
    int bx0 = menu->band[0], by0 = menu->band[1], bx1 = menu->band[2], by1 = menu->band[3];
    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
    {
        int x0, y0, x1, y1;
        if (menu->axis == GP_AXIS_H)
        {
            y0 = by0; y1 = by1;
            x0 = bx0 + gp_edge(c, bx1 - bx0, count);
            x1 = bx0 + gp_edge(c + 1, bx1 - bx0, count);
        }
        else
        {
            x0 = bx0; x1 = bx1;
            y0 = by0 + gp_edge(c, by1 - by0, count);
            y1 = by0 + gp_edge(c + 1, by1 - by0, count);
        }
        gp_rect_mean_bgr(frame, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, col[c]);
    }

    /* Normalize per frame: subtract per-channel mean across cells, divide by the
     * scalar spread (matches highlight.cell_colors in the prototype). */
    float mean[3] = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f};
    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] += col[c][ch]; }
    for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++) { mean[ch] /= (float)count; }

    double var = 0.0;
    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
        {
            double d = (double)col[c][ch] - (double)mean[ch];
            var += d * d;
        }
    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)(count * 3));
    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }

    int best = 0;
    float best_dev = -1.0f;
    for (int c = 0; c < count; c++)
    {
        const float *base = &menu->baseline[c * 3];
        float dev = 0.0f;
        for (int ch = 0; ch < 3; ch++)
        {
            float v = (col[c][ch] - mean[ch]) / std;
            float d = v - base[ch];
            dev += d * d;
        }
        if (dev > best_dev) { best_dev = dev; best = c; }
    }
    return best;
}

/* ── song_select ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Per-frame-normalized low-res luma grid over an ROI, offset by (dx,dy). */
static void gp_song_grid(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h,
                         const int roi[4], int dx, int dy, float *out)
{
    int x0 = roi[0] + dx, y0 = roi[1] + dy;
    int pw = roi[2] - roi[0], ph = roi[3] - roi[1];
    for (int r = 0; r < GP_SONG_ROWS; r++)
    {
        int cy0 = y0 + gp_edge(r, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
        int cy1 = y0 + gp_edge(r + 1, ph, GP_SONG_ROWS);
        if (cy0 < 0) { cy0 = 0; }  if (cy1 > h) { cy1 = h; }
        for (int c = 0; c < GP_SONG_COLS; c++)
        {
            int cx0 = x0 + gp_edge(c, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
            int cx1 = x0 + gp_edge(c + 1, pw, GP_SONG_COLS);
            if (cx0 < 0) { cx0 = 0; }  if (cx1 > w) { cx1 = w; }
            double s = 0.0; uint32_t n = 0u;
            for (int y = cy0; y < cy1; y++)
            {
                const uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w + (uint32_t)cx0) * GP_BPP;
                for (int x = cx0; x < cx1; x++)
                {
                    s += (double)p[0] * 29.0 + (double)p[1] * 150.0 + (double)p[2] * 77.0;
                    p += GP_BPP;
                    n++;
                }
            }
            out[r * GP_SONG_COLS + c] = (n != 0u) ? (float)(s / 256.0 / (double)n) : 0.0f;
        }
    }
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { sum += out[i]; }
    float mean = (float)(sum / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
    double var = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++)
    {
        double d = (double)out[i] - (double)mean;
        var += d * d;
    }
    float std = (float)sqrt(var / (double)GP_SONG_LEN);
    if (std < 1e-6f) { std = 1.0f; }
    for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { out[i] = (out[i] - mean) / std; }
}

/* Offset-search grids, both ROIs. Static — single observer-task caller. */
static float s_slot_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];
static float s_first_grids[GP_SONG_NDX * GP_SONG_NDY][GP_SONG_LEN];

int gp_read_song(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, gp_song_t *out)
{
    if (width != GP_CANON_W || height != GP_CANON_H)
    {
        out->setlist = 0; out->index = 0; out->tmpl = -1;
        return -1;
    }
    static const int slot_roi[4]  = GP_SONG_SLOT_ROI;
    static const int first_roi[4] = GP_SONG_FIRST_ROI;

    int noff = 0;
    for (int ix = 0; ix < GP_SONG_NDX; ix++)
        for (int iy = 0; iy < GP_SONG_NDY; iy++)
        {
            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, slot_roi,  gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_slot_grids[noff]);
            gp_song_grid(frame, width, height, first_roi, gp_song_dx[ix], gp_song_dy[iy], s_first_grids[noff]);
            noff++;
        }

    float best_d = 1e30f;
    int best_t = -1;
    for (int t = 0; t < GP_N_SONGS; t++)
    {
        const float *vec = gp_song_templates[t].vec;
        const float (*grids)[GP_SONG_LEN] =
            (gp_song_templates[t].roi_kind == GP_SONG_ROI_FIRST) ? s_first_grids : s_slot_grids;
        float tbest = 1e30f;
        for (int o = 0; o < noff; o++)
        {
            float d = 0.0f;
            for (int i = 0; i < GP_SONG_LEN; i++) { d += fabsf(grids[o][i] - vec[i]); }
            if (d < tbest) { tbest = d; }
        }
        if (tbest < best_d) { best_d = tbest; best_t = t; }
    }

    out->tmpl = (int16_t)best_t;
    out->setlist = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].setlist : 0;
    out->index = (best_t >= 0) ? gp_song_templates[best_t].index : 0;
    return 0;
}

```

The `GAME:` line fires on any screen-or-selection change (rate-limited to ~10 Hz):

Done. The observer now runs at **~5 Hz in the background**, with a **force-trigger** for closed-loop use.

## Changes

- **`GAME_OBSERVE_PERIOD_MS = 200`** (~5 Hz background). The task drains every frame from the queue (so video never backs up) but only classifies/reads ~5×/sec.
- **`GameplayEngine_RequestObservation()`** — sets a one-shot flag; the task processes the very next captured frame regardless of the rate gate, then clears it. Latency to a forced read is ≤ one frame (~16–18 ms at 60 Hz capture).

The rate gate is now: `if (!force && elapsed < period) skip; else { force = false; process }`.

## How the force-trigger fits the closed loop

That's precisely the M10 pattern: the controller sends a menu input via `FretboardLink_Send`, then calls `GameplayEngine_RequestObservation()` so it sees the resulting screen/selection within a frame instead of waiting up to 200 ms — exactly the "verify after acting" the nav doc requires.

I exposed it as a **public API rather than auto-hooking it into `FretboardLink_Send`** — the link also carries gameplay strums (where the observer isn't the consumer), so the caller decides when to trigger. _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 23:40:24Z)**_

It's **~5 Hz** — the `~` is doing real work. Here's the precise behavior:

- Tick rate is 1000 Hz, so `pdMS_TO_TICKS(200)` = exactly 200 ms — the *gate* threshold has no rounding error.
- But the observer only acts **on a captured frame**: the logic is "process the first frame that arrives ≥ 200 ms after the last processed one." So the real cadence is **quantized to the capture frame grid** (~16.7 ms at the 480p60 source), not free-running.

200 ms ÷ 16.7 ms ≈ 12 frames, so it lands on roughly every 12th frame ≈ **200–217 ms apart → ~4.6–5 Hz**, with up to one frame of phase jitter. It can't be *exactly* 5 Hz by construction — you can only sample a frame when one exists, so the frame period is the floor on quantization.

It's also a **ceiling, not a fixed rate**: if a song-screen classification+match takes, say, 50 ms, that's absorbed within the 200 ms window (start-to-start timing), so the cadence stays ~5 Hz; only if processing exceeded 200 ms would it stretch.

If you'd prefer I make the *intent* explicit, I can rename `GAME_OBSERVE_PERIOD_MS` / comment it as "minimum period between observations (≈5 Hz, quantized to frame arrivals)" so nobody later reads it as a guaranteed 5.000 Hz. Want that wording tweak, or leave it?

_**User (2026-06-15 23:43:04Z)**_

I guess what I'm asking is are we using the plain task delay that doesn't account for execution time of the task? Or the version that tracks tick of last execution? I forget function names but know that there's two different flavors of task delay?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 23:43:36Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 23:43:47Z)**_

Neither, actually — that's the thing to clarify. The two flavors you're thinking of are:

- **`vTaskDelay(n)`** — relative ("sleep n ticks *from now*"). Drifts, because the task's own execution time gets added on top each cycle.
- **`vTaskDelayUntil()` / `xTaskDelayUntil()`** — absolute ("wake at last-wake + n"). Fixed-frequency; it accounts for execution time by anchoring to the previous wake tick.

The observer uses **neither**. It's **event-driven**: the task blocks on `xQueueReceive(frames, …, portMAX_DELAY)` — it wakes on *every* captured frame — and then a manual gate decides whether to do work:

```c
now = xTaskGetTickCount();
if (!s_force_observe && (now - last_tick) < period) { continue; }  // drop this frame
s_force_observe = false;
last_tick = now;
/* classify + read … */
```

So the cadence is paced by frame arrivals, with a tick-comparison filter on top.

On your real question — execution-time accounting — note **`last_tick` is sampled at the *start* of the iteration** (before classify/read), and the gate compares *start-to-start*. So execution time is **absorbed within** the 200 ms window rather than added to it: a 50 ms song-match doesn't push the next observation to 250 ms. That gives it the **fixed-frequency behavior of `xTaskDelayUntil`, not the drift of `vTaskDelay`** — with the one caveat that, being frame-gated, the next observation is the first frame at ≥ `last_tick + period`, so it's quantized to the ~16.7 ms frame grid (bounded ≤ one-frame lag, no unbounded accumulation).

The only way it would stretch past ~5 Hz is if a single classify+read exceeded 200 ms — which it won't (worst case, the song match, is tens of ms).

If you'd rather the pacing be explicit/independent of the frame queue, I could restructure it to `xTaskDelayUntil` — but that'd mean either polling the latest frame or still gating on the queue, and the current frame-driven form is actually the cleaner fit here (it never spins, and it can't observe a stale/duplicate frame). Happy to switch if you prefer the explicit-period idiom.
